sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Early in the morning on August 17, 1999, an earthquake struck northwestern Turkey.
sentences.zh: 1999年8月17日清晨，土耳其西北部发生了一场地震。

sentences.en: It was the first of two earthquakes that would devastate that nation and parts of Greece.
sentences.zh: 这是将给该国以及希腊部分地区带来毁灭性打击的两场地震中的第一场。

sentences.en: Whole cities were reduced to rubble.
sentences.zh: 整座整座的城市沦为废墟。

sentences.en: Thousands of people were killed, and hundreds of thousands were left homeless.
sentences.zh: 数千人丧生，数十万人流离失所。

sentences.en: Amid the destruction, however, something extraordinary happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，在满目疮痍之中，发生了一件非同寻常的事。

sentences.en: Turkish rescue workers saved a Greek child from the wreckage of a building.
sentences.zh: 土耳其救援人员从一栋建筑的残骸中救出了一名希腊儿童。

sentences.en: A Greek man offered to donate a kidney to someone in Turkey.
sentences.zh: 一名希腊男子主动提出向土耳其的一位患者捐赠肾脏。

sentences.en: And the Greek foreign minister, George Papandreou, called on his fellow Greeks to offer aid.
sentences.zh: 希腊外长乔治·帕潘德里欧也呼吁同胞们提供援助。

sentences.en: I heard the news, and the media immediately asked me, have you sent a statement?
sentences.zh: 我听到这个消息后，媒体立刻问我：你发声明了吗？

sentences.en: And I said, you know, I sent a statement, but I want to say something more.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道的，我发了声明，但我还想说点别的。

sentences.en: Why don't we help the Turks?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不帮帮土耳其人呢？

sentences.en: Why don't we give blood?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不献血呢？

sentences.en: What made this remarkable is that Greece and Turkey have long had a rocky relationship,
sentences.zh: 最引人注目的是，希腊和土耳其长期以来关系紧张，

sentences.en: marked by periods of open warfare and animosity.
sentences.zh: 伴随着公开交火和敌对状态。

sentences.en: But George Papandreou saw an opportunity for rapprochement between the two nations.
sentences.zh: 但乔治·帕潘德里欧看到了两国实现和解的契机。

sentences.en: I felt this was a real issue, but it was also a political act.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个切实的议题，但它也是一种政治行为。

sentences.en: The idea of blood, of course, has a much deeper symbolism.
sentences.zh: 当然，血液的概念具有更深层的象征意义。

sentences.en: The interesting thing, which I hadn't expected, was there was an outpour of help.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我没有料到会有如此汹涌的援助之潮。

sentences.en: In the weeks that followed, the blood drive intervention and other aid efforts transformed the way many Greeks and Turks saw each other.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几周里，献血行动和其他救援努力改变了许多希腊人和土耳其人对彼此的看法。

sentences.en: They began to view each other not as enemies, but as fellow victims of a terrible disaster.
sentences.zh: 他们开始将对方视为可怕灾难中的同命人，而不再是敌人。

sentences.en: Very quickly, this sentiment spilled over into new domains.
sentences.zh: 很快，这种情绪蔓延到了新的领域。

sentences.en: So then all of a sudden, you saw things coming out which, you know, we would never expect it.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你会发现一些我们从未预料到的事情涌现出来。

sentences.en: So cookbooks that are Greek-Turkish cookbooks, of course.
sentences.zh: 比如希腊-土耳其合著的食谱，当然是这样。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: We have competitions, who makes better baklava?
sentences.zh: 我们有比赛，看谁能做出更好的果仁蜜饼？

sentences.en: Then we had TV serials where a Turkish man or a Turkish woman would fall in love with a Greek woman or a Greek man.
sentences.zh: 接着我们有了电视剧，讲的是土耳其男子或女子与希腊女子或男子坠入爱河。

sentences.en: And so there was a bit, you know, these, you know, soap operas that were, became very popular.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这些肥皂剧变得非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: The blood drive reframed the relationship.
sentences.zh: 献血行动重构了这种关系。

sentences.en: It was a psychological intervention, and it was powerful.
sentences.zh: 这是一次心理干预，而且力量强大。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to look at a similar psychological intervention.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨一场类似的心理干预。

sentences.en: It targets one of America's most pressing social challenges.
sentences.zh: 它直指美国最紧迫的社会挑战之一。

sentences.en: The way in which radical social change takes place is a step and a step and a step and then a fall.
sentences.zh: 激进社会变革的发生方式往往是一步、一步、又一步，然后是一次溃败。

sentences.en: How changing the frame around a problem can make the seemingly impossible possible.
sentences.zh: 如何改变围绕问题的框架，能让看似不可能的事情变为可能。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Most Americans have strong and automatic reactions to news reports involving police shootings.
sentences.zh: 大多数美国人对涉及警察枪击事件的新闻报道有着强烈且自动的反应。

sentences.en: Some of us are outraged.
sentences.zh: 我们当中有些人感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Some defensive.
sentences.zh: 有些人则充满防御心理。

sentences.en: All of us feel exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: It often feels like we are stuck between two camps.
sentences.zh: 人们常常觉得我们陷入了两个阵营之间。

sentences.en: One, that's outraged about the police.
sentences.zh: 一个是因警察而愤怒。

sentences.en: And another, that's outraged that we are outraged about the police.
sentences.zh: 另一个则是对我们因警察而愤怒而感到愤怒。

sentences.en: At Yale University, psychologist Philip Atiba Goff has come at the problem in a novel way.
sentences.zh: 在耶鲁大学，心理学家菲利普·阿蒂巴·戈夫以一种新颖的方式切入了这个问题。

sentences.en: His data show there are indeed racial disparities in how policing unfolds in many communities.
sentences.zh: 他的数据表明，在许多社区中，执法过程中的确存在种族差异。

sentences.en: Disparities tied not to the occurrence of crime or the prevalence of poverty, but the choices that police officers make.
sentences.zh: 这种差异并非源于犯罪率或贫困率，而是源于警员们的选择。

sentences.en: What makes his work unusual is how he thinks we should fix the problem.
sentences.zh: 他的工作之所以与众不同，在于他认为我们应当如何解决这个问题。

sentences.en: His novel approach has produced that rarest of things.
sentences.zh: 他新颖的方法催生了最罕见的事物。

sentences.en: Consensus between police and communities and actual change.
sentences.zh: 警方与社区之间的共识以及切实的改变。

sentences.en: Philip Atiba Goff, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·阿蒂巴·戈夫，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Philip, back in 2007, you were starting out as a young faculty member at Penn State.
sentences.zh: 菲利普，早在2007年时，你刚开始在宾夕法尼亚州立大学担任青年教员。

sentences.en: You attended a conference with academics and law enforcement officers.
sentences.zh: 你参加了一个由学者和执法人员出席的会议。

sentences.en: There was a well-dressed black woman sitting in the back of the room.
sentences.zh: 房间后排坐着一位衣着考究的黑人女性。

sentences.en: She was a senior officer in the Denver Police Department.
sentences.zh: 她是丹佛警察局的高级警官。

sentences.en: You went up to say hello to her, and she said something odd in response.
sentences.zh: 你走过去跟她打招呼，她却回了一句很奇怪的话。

sentences.en: What did she say?
sentences.zh: 她说了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I went up to her because she was sitting by herself, and I wanted to make her feel welcome.
sentences.zh: 是的，我走过去是因为她独自坐着，我想让她感到宾至如归。

sentences.en: So I asked if I could sit down.
sentences.zh: 所以我问我能不能坐下。

sentences.en: And she told me that I lacked the moral fortitude to do anything real with my life.
sentences.zh: 而她告诉我，我缺乏做任何真正有意义的事情的道德毅力。

sentences.en: So that's an odd thing to say to someone you're meeting for the first time.
sentences.zh: 对于一个初次见面的人来说，这话确实挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: The woman's name was Tracy Kazee, and she was essentially throwing down a challenge to you as an academic.
sentences.zh: 这位女士名叫特蕾西·卡齐，她实际上是对你这位学者发起了挑战。

sentences.en: Give me the context for her remark.
sentences.zh: 能讲讲她这番话的背景吗？

sentences.en: So there was a 15-year-old boy who was suffering from mental illness.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个患有精神疾病的15岁男孩。

sentences.en: He grabbed a knife, allegedly because he was frustrated he couldn't communicate with his family.
sentences.zh: 他抓起了一把刀，据说是因为无法与家人沟通而感到沮丧。

sentences.en: His family got scared.
sentences.zh: 他的家人吓坏了。

sentences.en: They called law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 他们报了警。

sentences.en: Law enforcement showed up and killed this boy in his own home.
sentences.zh: 执法人员赶到现场，并在男孩自己的家中将其击毙。

sentences.en: At a town hall meeting that followed, an African-American woman asked Tracy,
sentences.zh: 在随后召开的市民大会上，一名非裔美国女性问特蕾西，

sentences.en: do you train your officers to kill young black men?
sentences.zh: 你们训练警官去杀死年轻的黑人男性吗？

sentences.en: And this is a slam dunk from a PR perspective.
sentences.zh: 从公关的角度来看，这是一个稳赢的问题。

sentences.en: It's an easy question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: You just say no and move on.
sentences.zh: 你只要说不，然后继续就行了。

sentences.en: But because of who Tracy is, she actually heard the question.
sentences.zh: 但由于特蕾西的性格，她实实在在地听进去了这个问题。

sentences.en: She wanted to know the answer.
sentences.zh: 她想要知道答案。

sentences.en: And she realized and then said out loud, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 她意识到并大声说出了口：我不知道。

sentences.en: So after that incident, she spent the next two years trying to figure out who could help her answer that question.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个事件之后，她在接下来的两年里试图弄清楚谁能帮她回答这个问题。

sentences.en: She wanted someone to work with who would not care about how long it took to get the answers.
sentences.zh: 她想找一个不在乎花多久时间来寻找答案的人合作。

sentences.en: And she was frustrated, I think, by the fact that the academy was not set up to help people answer those kinds of questions.
sentences.zh: 我想，她对学术界没有建立起帮助人们解答这类问题的机制感到沮丧。

sentences.en: So she found me and we began to try and answer not just that question,
sentences.zh: 所以她找到了我，我们开始尝试回答不仅是那个问题，

sentences.en: but the deeper questions of what do you do with the reality of racism in the context of public safety?
sentences.zh: 还有更深层次的问题：在公共安全的背景下，你该如何面对种族主义这一现实？

sentences.en: The boy who was killed was Paul Childs, and the incident happened in Denver in 2003.
sentences.zh: 被杀害的男孩名叫保罗·柴尔兹，事件于2003年发生在丹佛。

sentences.en: Philip and Tracy said, I don't know, to the question,
sentences.zh: 菲利普和特蕾西对这个问题说出了“我不知道”，

sentences.en: does your police department train officers to kill young black men?
sentences.zh: 你们的警察部门是否训练警官去杀死年轻的黑人男性？

sentences.en: What I'm hearing is that she felt there might be something structural embedded in police practices
sentences.zh: 我的理解是，她觉得警务实践中可能潜藏着某种结构性问题，

sentences.en: that made it more likely that an officer might kill a young black man?
sentences.zh: 使得警官更有可能杀死年轻的黑人男性？

sentences.en: It wasn't just, hey, yeah, maybe there's some structural stuff going on.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是说，嘿，对啊，也许存在一些结构性问题。

sentences.en: Maybe the training is having this unintended consequence.
sentences.zh: 也许这种培训产生了这种意料之外的后果。

sentences.en: It was how on earth have we been doing this in this country for 100 plus years?
sentences.zh: 而是我们到底是怎么在这个国家把这事干了一百多年的？

sentences.en: We haven't bothered to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至懒得去回答这个问题。

sentences.en: And in most places, we haven't bothered to ask it of the people who have the capacity to make sure there's an answer.
sentences.zh: 而且在大多数地方，我们甚至懒得去质问那些有能力确保给出答案的人。

sentences.en: There's a kind of neglect, a negligence in the way that we've asked questions of our public safety
sentences.zh: 我们在对公共安全提出质问的方式中存在一种忽视、一种玩忽职守，

sentences.en: that reveals that we haven't centered the experiences of the people who fear getting killed
sentences.zh: 这表明我们没有把那些害怕被回应危机报警电话的人枪杀的群体置于核心地位。

sentences.en: by the folks who respond when you call out in crisis.
sentences.zh: 当你在危机中呼叫救援时。

sentences.en: That was a lot of the frustration that I know that she felt in that moment.
sentences.zh: 我知道这正是她当时感到的挫败感所在。

sentences.en: In the years since that meeting, you and Tracy Kazee have set up a national organization.
sentences.zh: 在那次会面之后的几年里，你和特蕾西·卡齐建立了一个全国性组织。

sentences.en: We're going to talk at length about the work you've done,
sentences.zh: 我们将详细讨论你们所做的工作，

sentences.en: but I want to start by establishing the context for your work.
sentences.zh: 但我首先想为你们的工作确立一个背景。

sentences.en: Many of us feel a sense of hopelessness when we hear about discrimination and policing.
sentences.zh: 当我们听到有关歧视和警务的新闻时，许多人会感到一种绝望感。

sentences.en: You say that one reason for this hopelessness is that for the last 250 years,
sentences.zh: 你说这种绝望感的原因之一是，在过去的250年里，

sentences.en: we have defined the problem wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们把问题定义错了。

sentences.en: We have defined the problem in a way that effectively makes the problem unsolvable.
sentences.zh: 我们对问题的定义实际上让这个问题变得无法解决。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: So if the problem is individual character inside hearts and minds, a defect of the soul that we've
sentences.zh: 因此，如果问题出在心灵深处的个人品格上，出在我们必须修复的灵魂缺陷上，

sentences.en: got to fix, there are many problems with that.
sentences.zh: 那么这样做会带来许多问题。

sentences.en: The first of which, of course, is that it doesn't track particularly closely with the science.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个问题当然是，它与科学并不十分吻合。

sentences.en: But probably more importantly, it's just a hard problem to fix.
sentences.zh: 但可能更重要的是，这本身就是一个很难解决的问题。

sentences.en: And then we're having a conversation about a thing that is almost impossible to reliably measure.
sentences.zh: 而且我们现在讨论的是一个几乎无法进行可靠测量的事物。

sentences.en: There's no saliva test to be like, nope, you're 45% racist, so now you definitely got to go to the
sentences.zh: 没有什么唾液测试能告诉你：不，你含有45%的种族主义，所以你现在绝对得去

sentences.en: re-education center.
sentences.zh: 再教育中心。

sentences.en: There's no way to really know.
sentences.zh: 根本没有办法真正知道。

sentences.en: And even if you could, then you've maybe fixed the one person.
sentences.zh: 即便你能做到，那你也许只是修复了一个人。

sentences.en: And that's not going to work across 18,000 law enforcement agencies in this country.
sentences.zh: 这在全国18,000个执法机构中是行不通的。

sentences.en: And that's just law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 而且这还只是执法部门。

sentences.en: Forget about everybody who's got access to 911 and can use law enforcement as their personal
sentences.zh: 更不用说那些能够拨打911并利用执法部门作为他们私人

sentences.en: racism concierge.
sentences.zh: 种族主义礼宾服务的所有人了。

sentences.en: So it creates layers of difficulty at solving the problem, from the difficulty detecting it
sentences.zh: 因此，它从检测的难度到真正改变人心和思想的能力，

sentences.en: to the ability to actually change hearts and minds.
sentences.zh: 在解决问题方面制造了层层阻碍。

sentences.en: And that is exhausting when you look at how often we have racism producing outcomes that
sentences.zh: 当你看到种族主义产生的悲剧性后果如此频繁时，这会让人筋疲力尽，

sentences.en: are so tragic as to make you have to shut down your whole life for a day or a week or
sentences.zh: 以至于你不得不把整个人生停摆一天、一周、

sentences.en: a month or longer.
sentences.zh: 一个月甚至更久。

sentences.en: Forget about the country.
sentences.zh: 更别提整个国家了。

sentences.en: I want to look at three examples from the news that illustrate how we have long thought about
sentences.zh: 我想看一看新闻中的三个例子，它们说明了我们长期以来是如何看待

sentences.en: the problem of disparities in policing.
sentences.zh: 警务中存在差异这一问题的。

sentences.en: Later in the show, we look at how redefining the problem can help us rethink those challenges.
sentences.zh: 在节目的后面部分，我们将探讨重新定义问题如何能帮助我们重新思考这些挑战。

sentences.en: In March of 2021, two police officers responded to reports of gunfire in the Chicago neighborhood
sentences.zh: 2021年3月，两名警官赶往芝加哥小村庄社区应对枪击报告。

sentences.en: Little Village.
sentences.zh: 小村庄。

sentences.en: They chased a suspect, Adam Toledo, down a dark alley.
sentences.zh: 他们在一条黑暗的巷子里追逐一名嫌疑人亚当·托莱多。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened next?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我接下来发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Adam Toledo was a boy.
sentences.zh: 亚当·托莱多还是个孩子。

sentences.en: He was hanging out with somebody else who allegedly had fired a gun.
sentences.zh: 他当时和另一个人在一起，那个人据称曾开枪射击。

sentences.en: That individual was closer to adulthood, handed the gun to Adam Toledo, who ran away.
sentences.zh: 那个人年纪更大一些，把枪交给了亚当·托莱多，后者随后逃跑。

sentences.en: And then when realizing that law enforcement was close, tried to dispose of the gun in a way
sentences.zh: 然后，当意识到执法人员逼近时，他试图通过某种方式处理掉这把枪，

sentences.en: that he wouldn't get in trouble.
sentences.zh: 这样他就不会惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: The officer saw the gun, saw it flash and move, and then killed Adam Toledo.
sentences.zh: 警官看到了枪，看到它闪光并移动，随后开枪打死了亚当·托莱多。

sentences.en: I remember there was a huge debate about the case.
sentences.zh: 我记得围绕这个案件曾有过一场巨大的争论。

sentences.en: Some people said, shooting a 13-year-old child, simply unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 有些人说，枪杀一个13岁的儿童，简直是不可接受的。

sentences.en: Nothing more to discuss.
sentences.zh: 没什么好讨论的。

sentences.en: Others said, hang on.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则说，等等。

sentences.en: The police could not have known that he was 13, and Adam Toledo looked like he was armed.
sentences.zh: 警察不可能知道他只有13岁，而且亚当·托莱多看起来像是武装了。

sentences.en: The officer had to make a split-second decision.
sentences.zh: 警官必须在电光石火之间做出决定。

sentences.en: He did not know if Adam Toledo was raising his arms to surrender or raising his arms to
sentences.zh: 他不知道亚当·托莱多举起双手是为了投降，还是为了

sentences.en: open fire.
sentences.zh: 开枪还击。

sentences.en: So each side not only feels they are right, but that the other is unsympathetic, irrational,
sentences.zh: 因此，每一方不仅觉得自己是正确的，还觉得对方缺乏同理心、不讲理，

sentences.en: maybe even evil.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是邪恶的。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.

sentences.en: And that bigger racism is driving some of these disparities.
sentences.zh: 正是这种更大范围的种族主义在推动其中一些差异。

sentences.en: So what part belongs to the police and what part doesn't?
sentences.zh: 那么，哪一部分归咎于警察，哪一部分不归咎于警察？

sentences.en: The answer is simply, poverty and crime are insufficient to explain racial disparities
sentences.zh: 答案很简单，贫困和犯罪不足以解释警察在武力使用、

sentences.en: in police use of force, stops, arrests, or other burdensome police behaviors.
sentences.zh: 拦截、逮捕或其他繁重执法行为中存在的种族差异。

sentences.en: What we see is that black folks across the country are about four times more likely to have force used on them than white folks.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，全国各地的黑人群体遭受武力对待的可能性大约是白人群体的四倍。

sentences.en: When you control for crime and poverty, black folks are, in our data, somewhere between one and a half times as likely.
sentences.zh: 在控制了犯罪和贫困变量后，在我们的数据中，黑人群体遭遇武力的可能性大约是一倍半。

sentences.en: And 16 times as likely.
sentences.zh: 甚至是16倍。

sentences.en: Sometimes it gets worse because of the spatial distribution of law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 由于执法力度的空间分布，有时情况会变得更糟。

sentences.en: So, Philip, when we look at data like that, it's easy to conclude that racism has to be behind these disparities.
sentences.zh: 所以，菲利普，当我们看到这样的数据时，很容易得出种族主义必然是这些差异背后的原因的结论。

sentences.en: But you once wrote, there is mounting evidence that racial discrimination can occur even absent racial bigotry, either overt or covert.
sentences.zh: 但你曾经写道：越来越多的证据表明，即使在没有显性或隐性种族偏见的情况下，种族歧视也可能发生。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so I just want to reframe just a little bit that question.
sentences.zh: 因此，我只想稍微重新界定一下那个问题。

sentences.en: It is racism.
sentences.zh: 这是种族主义。

sentences.en: It just doesn't have to be bigotry.
sentences.zh: 它只是不一定非得是偏执。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Bigotry and prejudice, that's inside.
sentences.zh: 偏执和偏见，那是内心层面的。

sentences.en: I want us to get that racism is that pattern of behaviors out in the world.
sentences.zh: 我想让我们明白，种族主义是世界上存在的某种行为模式。

sentences.en: So, for instance, when a family is dealing with someone who is in the midst of a mental health crisis,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，当一个家庭在应对某个正处于心理健康危机中的成员时，

sentences.en: they may try and talk to someone.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会试着和某人谈谈。

sentences.en: They may try and reach out for help to someone at a hospital.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会试着向医院的工作人员寻求帮助。

sentences.en: They may try and set something up for a clinic.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会试着为诊所安排点什么。

sentences.en: When that family member who is in mental distress doesn't want to go, we don't have any resources that are available to the public to help out.
sentences.zh: 当那个处于心理痛苦中的家庭成员不想去时，我们没有任何可供公众使用的资源来提供帮助。

sentences.en: And what that means is that people who have a lot of money have other folks they can call.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，那些很有钱的人有其他人可以打电话求助。

sentences.en: They can spend money on private therapy.
sentences.zh: 他们可以花钱进行私人治疗。

sentences.en: They can spend money for, you know, family counseling.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们可以花钱进行家庭咨询。

sentences.en: And people without money, the only place they have to call when it gets really bad is 911.
sentences.zh: 而没钱的人，情况变得非常糟糕时，他们唯一能拨打的电话就是911。

sentences.en: And 911 has three options.
sentences.zh: 而911有三个选项。

sentences.en: A fire, ambulance, or a badge and a gun.
sentences.zh: 火警、救护车，或者警徽和枪支。

sentences.en: And so that's how, without needing to dislike black people, it may, in fact, be black family members, as it was in the case of Paul Childs, who cry out for help.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么在不需要厌恶黑人的情况下，事实可能正是黑人家庭成员在呼救——正如保罗·查尔斯（Paul Childs）的情况一样。

sentences.en: But the way we have structured the system says that the folks who have the least don't get the set of options and resources that would prevent them from needing our systems of punishment to come and take the place of the systems we should have for care.
sentences.zh: 但我们构建系统的方式表明，那些最一无所有的人，得不到那些能够阻止他们陷入惩罚体系的选项和资源——本该用来替代关怀体系的惩罚体系。

sentences.en: Now, we talked earlier about your meeting with Tracy Kazee.
sentences.zh: 此前，我们谈到了你与特蕾西·卡齐（Tracy Kazee）的会面。

sentences.en: The two of you started an organization called the Center for Policing Equity.
sentences.zh: 你们两个创办了一个名为“警务公平中心”的组织。

sentences.en: And you wanted the focus to be not on what's happening inside the hearts and minds of police officers, but on what they do.
sentences.zh: 你们希望人们关注的焦点不是警官内心的想法，而是他们的行为。

sentences.en: You say there's a long precedent for this idea in policing, at least when it comes to combating crime.
sentences.zh: 你说过，在警务工作中，这种理念有着悠久的先例，至少在打击犯罪方面是这样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I wish that I had figured out earlier that there was a really easy way for everyone who's ever worked in an organization to understand it.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能早点发现，对于所有在组织里工作过的人来说，有一种非常简单的方式来理解这一点。

sentences.en: It's just performance management.
sentences.zh: 这就是绩效管理。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: It's nothing more fancy than that.
sentences.zh: 没有比这更花哨的了。

sentences.en: In law enforcement, what they've done for the last, you know, more than a quarter century is they've measured crime.
sentences.zh: 在执法部门，你知道的，在过去的二十多年里，他们一直在衡量犯罪情况。

sentences.en: And about 80% of law enforcement agencies use something like what's called CompStat.
sentences.zh: 大约80%的执法机构都在使用类似于“CompStat”（犯罪统计）的东西。

sentences.en: But in its purest form, the idea is you should be paying attention to crime if your goal is to prevent it.
sentences.zh: 但从最纯粹的形式来看，这个理念是：如果你的目标是预防犯罪，你就应该关注犯罪。

sentences.en: You should be looking for patterns.
sentences.zh: 你应该寻找规律。

sentences.en: And then when you're done finding the patterns, you should be trying to hold yourself accountable for driving down the rates of crime.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你找出规律后，你就应该努力让自己承担起降低犯罪率的责任。

sentences.en: That's performance management 101 in any organization.
sentences.zh: 这是任何组织中绩效管理的基础知识。

sentences.en: What do you want to get done?
sentences.zh: 你想完成什么？

sentences.en: What do you want to avoid?
sentences.zh: 你想避免什么？

sentences.en: Track it.
sentences.zh: 追踪它。

sentences.en: Hold people accountable to it.
sentences.zh: 让人们对此负责。

sentences.en: So let's see how we can apply this model of performance evaluation to reducing discrimination in policing.
sentences.zh: 因此，让我们来看看如何将这种绩效评估模式应用到减少警务歧视中。

sentences.en: In 2011, you got a call from the Las Vegas Police Department.
sentences.zh: 2011年，你接到了拉斯维加斯警察局的电话。

sentences.en: They were confronting accusations that they used force too often.
sentences.zh: 他们当时面临着过度使用武力的指控。

sentences.en: Now, instead of saying, let's examine the character of the officers in the department, of course, that's hard to measure, hard to change.
sentences.zh: 现在，与其说让我们检查该部门警官的品格——当然，这很难衡量，也很难改变。

sentences.en: It's a bad metric for performance evaluation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个用于绩效评估的糟糕指标。

sentences.en: You looked at the data and found something tangible that could be measured and could be changed.
sentences.zh: 你查看了数据，并发现了一些可以衡量和改变的实际切入点。

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: What we found is that after foot pursuits, we saw a higher rate of use of force across the board.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在步行追捕之后，我们看到各方面使用武力的比率都有所上升。

sentences.en: Now, foot pursuit is when someone runs away and the officer takes chase on foot.
sentences.zh: 现在，步行追捕是指有人逃跑，警官在步行追赶。

sentences.en: It's not that complicated.
sentences.zh: 这并不复杂。

sentences.en: But it's pretty easy when you go back to someone and you say, well, what does that feel like?
sentences.zh: 但当你回头问某人时，这其实很容易理解：那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: To understand why you get higher rates of force.
sentences.zh: 从而理解为什么你们会获得更高频率的武力使用。

sentences.en: Because you took off, so I'm running after you.
sentences.zh: 因为你逃跑了，所以我才在后面追你。

sentences.en: That means my heart rate is up.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我的心率上升了。

sentences.en: My adrenaline is going.
sentences.zh: 我的肾上腺素在飙升。

sentences.en: I know you're a bad guy because who runs from the cops like bad guys in the minds of officers.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是个坏人，因为在警察的心目中，逃跑的人就像坏人。

sentences.en: And then if you go around a corner, maybe you have a gun around the corner or there's a friend who's there to hurt me.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果你转过一个拐角，拐角处可能有一把枪，或者那里有个朋友来伤害我。

sentences.en: So even if you turn around and you say, hey, please don't hurt me and put your hands up, you might be getting a shot to the kidneys for the price of making me run.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你转过身来说，嘿，请不要伤害我，并把双手举起来，你可能会因为让我不得不奔跑而挨上一记肾上腺素飙升的重击。

sentences.en: And so the result in Las Vegas, once we gave that back to law enforcement and back to the community, they said, hey, could you guys just literally take a breath?
sentences.zh: 因此，在拉斯维加斯，一旦我们将这一结果反馈给执法部门和社区，他们就会说，嘿，你们能字面意义上深呼吸一下吗？

sentences.en: And that was the comment.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的评论。

sentences.en: That was the spirit that made the change.
sentences.zh: 这就是促成改变的精神。

sentences.en: They said, yeah, we really probably should.
sentences.zh: 他们说，是的，我们确实应该这样做。

sentences.en: So let's train differently.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们进行不同的训练。

sentences.en: Let's tell folks that they shouldn't touch someone until backup has arrived.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉大家，在支援到达之前，不要触碰任何人。

sentences.en: They should count to 10 like everybody learns in their marriage counseling.
sentences.zh: 他们应该像每个人在婚姻咨询中学到的一样数到10。

sentences.en: Do the things to de-escalate your body so you don't end up engaging in unnecessary use of force.
sentences.zh: 做那些能让你的身体平静下来的事情，这样你就不会最终卷入不必要的武力使用中。

sentences.en: That's the language of law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 这就是执法部门的语言。

sentences.en: And the following year, we saw a significant decrease in use of force.
sentences.zh: 第二年，我们看到武力的使用显著下降。

sentences.en: My memory is it was 23% that following year and became a national model for how you do experience-based training, all of which goes back to, hey, what's the behavior?
sentences.zh: 我的记忆中，随后的那一年下降了23%，并成为如何开展体验式培训的国家典范，这一切都可以追溯到：嘿，行为是什么？

sentences.en: What do we think causes the behavior?
sentences.zh: 我们认为是什么导致了这种行为？

sentences.en: What's approximate to the behavior?
sentences.zh: 什么与这种行为密切相关？

sentences.en: Can we make a change in the thing that makes that happen that will reduce the incidence of the behavior?
sentences.zh: 我们能否改变导致这一结果的事物，从而减少这种行为的发生率？

sentences.en: I mean, this takes us back to what happened when we discussed the Adam Toledo shooting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这把我们带回了讨论亚当·托莱多（Adam Toledo）枪击案时发生的事情。

sentences.en: Two people are running.
sentences.zh: 两个人正在奔跑。

sentences.en: It's a dark alley.
sentences.zh: 这是一个黑暗的小巷。

sentences.en: They're both frightened.
sentences.zh: 他们都很害怕。

sentences.en: They can't see very well.
sentences.zh: 他们看不清。

sentences.en: And they have to make split-second, high-stakes decisions.
sentences.zh: 他们必须在电光石火之间做出高风险的决定。

sentences.en: Do this kind of thing regularly.
sentences.zh: 经常做这种事情。

sentences.en: And, of course, bad things will occur.
sentences.zh: 当然，糟糕的事情就会发生。

sentences.en: Now, I want to draw attention to what happens when you don't focus attention on the character of the police officer.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想提请大家注意，当你不再把注意力集中在警官的品格上时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Instead of saying, bad cops shoot kids, if you say, hey, look, foot pursuits increase the risk of tragic mistakes.
sentences.zh: 与其说“坏警察枪击儿童”，不如说“嘿，你看，步行追捕增加了悲惨错误的风险”。

sentences.en: Let's try and reduce the number of tragic mistakes in our department.
sentences.zh: 让我们试着减少我们部门中悲惨错误的数量。

sentences.en: Now, suddenly, cops and community don't find themselves on opposite sides of the equation.
sentences.zh: 现在，突然之间，警察和社区发现自己不再处于对立的立场。

sentences.en: They find themselves on the same page.
sentences.zh: 他们发现自己达成了一致。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in negotiations and international relations and in business, we talk about the difference between interests and positions.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在谈判、国际关系和商业中，我们都会谈到利益和立场的区别。

sentences.en: So a position is a thing you've got to defend, right?
sentences.zh: 所以立场是你必须捍卫的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: If I say, hey, no one can have their shoes on in my house, you've got a hole in your sock.
sentences.zh: 如果我说，嘿，在我的屋子里谁也不能穿鞋，而你的袜子破了个洞。

sentences.en: You're like, well, I guess I'm not coming in.
sentences.zh: 你就会想，好吧，那我想我不进去了。

sentences.en: But if I say, hey, this is a rug that my parents gave me.
sentences.zh: 但如果我说，嘿，这是一块我父母送给我的地毯。

sentences.en: It's been in the family for a long time.
sentences.zh: 它在家族里传了很久了。

sentences.en: It's real fragile.
sentences.zh: 它真的很脆弱。

sentences.en: We ask people to take their shoes off so that we don't mess up the rug.
sentences.zh: 我们请大家脱鞋是为了不把地毯弄坏。

sentences.en: Be like, hey, can I walk around the rug?
sentences.zh: 你就会说，嘿，我能绕着地毯走吗？

sentences.en: I'll be like, oh, yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 我会说，哦，当然可以。

sentences.en: Come in the back door.
sentences.zh: 从后门进来吧。

sentences.en: We can fix this.
sentences.zh: 我们可以解决这个问题。

sentences.en: We can work this out.
sentences.zh: 我们可以商量着办。

sentences.en: Because there are so many assumptions built into the way we talk about racism, we end up establishing positions before we've even listened to anybody's interests.
sentences.zh: 由于我们在谈论种族主义时内置了太多的假设，我们最终在甚至还没有倾听任何人的利益之前，就已经确立了各自的立场。

sentences.en: And so the thing that was shocking to me, because I'm a black dude from Philly, I figured when I showed up talking to law enforcement,
sentences.zh: 因此，让我感到震惊的是——因为我是费城的一个黑人小伙子——我想象当我去找执法部门谈话时，

sentences.en: I would find out that racist racists did racist things.
sentences.zh: 我会发现持种族主义观点的种族主义者做了种族主义的事情。

sentences.en: That's still true.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是真的。

sentences.en: But the majority of folks I encountered were like, oh, we get asked to do too much stuff.
sentences.zh: 但我遇到的大多数人都觉得，哦，我们被要求做太多事情了。

sentences.en: And we're definitely going to catch hell in the press and from communities that we really care about in large part because we get asked to do stuff we should never get asked to do.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对会在媒体和我们真正关心的社区那里挨骂，很大一部分原因是我们被要求去做那些本不该让我们去做的事。

sentences.en: And so when you compare the requests that I've received from law enforcement over the last 20-plus years to the requests that I hear from activists, they look really similar.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你把我过去20多年里从执法部门收到的请求与我从激进分子那里听到的请求进行比较时，它们看起来非常相似。

sentences.en: Law enforcement says get us out of mental health.
sentences.zh: 执法部门说，把我们从心理健康事务中解放出来。

sentences.en: Get us out of substance abuse.
sentences.zh: 把我们从戒毒事务中解放出来。

sentences.en: Get us out of child welfare.
sentences.zh: 把我们从儿童福利事务中解放出来。

sentences.en: Like, remove us out of the schools.
sentences.zh: 比如，把我们从学校里撤出来。

sentences.en: Don't ask us to be on suicide watch.
sentences.zh: 不要要求我们去进行防自杀监控。

sentences.en: Set up resources so that these communities that are blighted by crime have the thing so they don't have to engage in crime in the first place.
sentences.zh: 建立资源，让这些饱受犯罪祸害的社区拥有他们所需的东西，这样他们一开始就不必涉足犯罪。

sentences.en: If I were to tell you that came out of the mouth of an abolitionist, you wouldn't be surprised.
sentences.zh: 如果我告诉你这话出自一个废奴主义者之口，你不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: The major difference is law enforcement doesn't usually argue that they should get less money.
sentences.zh: 主要的区别在于，执法部门通常不会争辩说他们应该得到更少的资金。

sentences.en: And activists right about now are arguing for that quite loudly.
sentences.zh: 而激进分子现在正为此进行相当大声的争论。

sentences.en: But the substantive policy changes outside of law enforcement have a lot of support from law enforcement veterans,
sentences.zh: 但执法部门以外的实质性政策变化得到了许多资深执法人员的大力支持，

sentences.en: which I think is especially surprising to folks who are just hearing the national conversation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于刚刚听到全国性对话的人来说尤其令人惊讶。

sentences.en: A few years after his work in Las Vegas, Philip and his team began studying another idea.
sentences.zh: 在拉斯维加斯的工作几年后，菲利普和他的团队开始研究另一个想法。

sentences.en: Think back to the case involving Dante Wright.
sentences.zh: 回想一下丹特·赖特（Dante Wright）案。

sentences.en: Shortly after that shooting, people spent a lot of time arguing about whether the police officer who pulled the trigger acted out of malice.
sentences.zh: 在那起枪击案发生后不久，人们花了大量时间争论那个扣动扳机的警察是否出于恶意。

sentences.en: Few people stopped to ask a more basic question.
sentences.zh: 很少有人停下来问一个更基本的问题。

sentences.en: Should armed police officers be pulling over drivers for expired tags?
sentences.zh: 武装警察是否应该仅仅因为车牌过期就把司机拦在路边？

sentences.en: Turned out, this was also a question both the local community and the police were pondering in California.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这也是加州当地社区和警方都在思考的一个问题。

sentences.en: The Berkeley police chief reached out in part because of pressure from communities in Berkeley, California.
sentences.zh: 伯克利警察局长主动联系，部分原因来自加州伯克利社区的压力。

sentences.en: And they had the idea to look at what are we doing on traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 他们萌生了一个想法，即看看我们在交通拦截方面到底在做什么。

sentences.en: If you've got a lot of physical violence in a place that would never have happened if you didn't show up, the best solution might be don't show up.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个地方造成了大量的身体暴力，而如果不是你出现本不会发生这种暴力，那么最好的解决方案可能就是不要出现。

sentences.en: The old joke is, hey, doc, it hurts when I go like this.
sentences.zh: 旧笑话是，嘿，医生，我这么做的时候很痛。

sentences.en: Doc says, don't go like that.
sentences.zh: 医生说，那就别那么做。

sentences.en: And in Berkeley, they decided any low-level traffic enforcement, let us mail you a ticket because that's going to be safer for the officer.
sentences.zh: 在伯克利，他们决定对于任何低级别的交通执法，让我们把罚单寄给你，因为这对警官来说更安全。

sentences.en: It's going to be safer for the resident.
sentences.zh: 对居民来说也会更安全。

sentences.en: And likely nobody dies from a paper cut.
sentences.zh: 而且大概没有人会因为纸划伤而死。

sentences.en: To be clear, Philip is not saying there is never room for armed police.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，菲利普并不是说武装警察永远没有存在的空间。

sentences.en: He's saying, ask yourself if an officer with a badge and a gun needs to be your first response to a problem.
sentences.zh: 他是说，问问你自己，一个带着警徽和枪的警察是否需要成为你对某个问题的第一反应。

sentences.en: If someone is driving around with expired tags and you can send them a ticket in the mail, they might just pay the fine and get their tags renewed.
sentences.zh: 如果有人开着车牌过期的车到处转悠，而你可以把罚单寄到他们家里，他们可能就会直接付罚金并去更新车牌了。

sentences.en: Problem solved.
sentences.zh: 问题解决。

sentences.en: If they don't respond to the ticket, you can then think of escalating your response.
sentences.zh: 如果他们对罚单置之不理，你再考虑升级应对措施。

sentences.en: The very same principle applies to the use of no-knock warrants.
sentences.zh: 同样的原则也适用于“不敲门搜查令”的使用。

sentences.en: Philip told me about a local jurisdiction in New York that asked for help.
sentences.zh: 菲利普告诉我，纽约的一个地方司法辖区寻求了帮助。

sentences.en: We got involved with Ithaca and Tompkins County that wanted to do this together.
sentences.zh: 我们参与了伊萨卡和汤普金斯县的工作，他们希望共同完成这件事。

sentences.en: And so it was really important.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很重要。

sentences.en: It is really their work that we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里讨论的确实是他们的工作。

sentences.en: They brought school-age kids in to hear about their experiences and to say, well, how, if we wanted to start over, start from scratch, how, what would that look like?
sentences.zh: 他们把适龄学童请来倾听他们的经历，并询问：如果我们想重新开始，从头来过，那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: If we were really focused on protecting folks who were vulnerable, what systems would we build?
sentences.zh: 如果我们真正专注于保护弱势群体，我们会建立什么样的系统？

sentences.en: And it turns out that when you start that exercise, you don't start with police.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，当你开始这项练习时，你并不是从警察开始的。

sentences.en: You don't start with folks who have the ability to dole out violence in order to get compliance with the law.
sentences.zh: 你并不是从那些有能力施加暴力以迫使人们服从法律的人开始的。

sentences.en: You start with the basic necessities of living.
sentences.zh: 你是从生活的基本需求开始的。

sentences.en: And so the communities in Ithaca and Tompkins County said, well, we're going to want folks who can respond to violence,
sentences.zh: 因此，伊萨卡和汤普金斯县的社区表示，好吧，我们会需要能够应对暴力的人，

sentences.en: but we want them directed by folks who are thinking about community solutions to public safety that will often not require law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 但我们希望他们听从那些思考公共安全社区解决方案的人的指挥，而这些方案通常不需要执法部门介入。

sentences.en: And along with that are a set of recommendations, including, yeah, we shouldn't have no-knock warrants.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一系列建议，其中包括：是的，我们不应该有“不敲门搜查令”。

sentences.en: Like, we should be a community that knows who lives here well enough that we don't have to resort to the element of surprise to deal with folks who are damaging the communities.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们应该成为一个足够了解这里居民的社区，以至于我们不必诉诸突袭的元素来对付那些破坏社区的人。

sentences.en: And when the community wants those folks to stop their behavior or even to be taken out of it.
sentences.zh: 当社区希望那些人停止他们的行为，甚至将他们带离该环境时。

sentences.en: You know, Philip, in some ways I'm struck by the fact that what you're advocating, and no disrespect here, it's actually not rocket science.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，菲利普，在某些方面，我感触很深的是，你所倡导的——这里绝无不敬之意——其实并不是什么高深莫测的科学。

sentences.en: It's almost common sense.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就是常识。

sentences.en: If you want to reduce the risk that the police will shoot someone by mistake, the first thing to do is don't send armed police to situations that don't require armed police.
sentences.zh: 如果你想降低警察误杀平民的风险，首先要做的事情就是，不要把武装警察派去不需要武装警察的场合。

sentences.en: So the hard part here is figuring out the interests and figuring out where is there room to move.
sentences.zh: 所以这里最难的部分，是摸清各方的利益诉求，并找出还有多少妥协的空间。

sentences.en: Where can we get collaboration, coalition, consensus to move us forward?
sentences.zh: 我们在哪里可以达成合作、建立联盟、凝聚共识，从而推动我们向前发展？

sentences.en: I say all the time, why are we bringing a badge and a gun to a place where someone's thinking about ending their own life?
sentences.zh: 我经常说，当某人正萌生轻生念头时，我们为什么偏要带著警徽和枪支去现场？

sentences.en: Philip cites a case where officers were called to a home where a man was pointing a gun at his own head.
sentences.zh: 菲利普举了一个例子：当时有警员接到报警来到一处住宅，一名男子正拿枪指着自己的头部。

sentences.en: And the police said, that's a danger to us, and shot and killed him.
sentences.zh: 而警察却说，这构成了对我们的威胁，于是开枪把他打死了。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That's a tragedy on top of tragedy.
sentences.zh: 这是悲剧中的悲剧。

sentences.en: The family is concerned that this person is going to die and then calls the state and the state shows up and does it for him.
sentences.zh: 家属原本担心这个人会自杀，于是报警求助，结果国家派人来帮他把这事给办了。

sentences.en: But I wish it were the case that if you don't introduce a gun, the chance of getting shot were zero.
sentences.zh: 但我多么希望只要不带枪，中枪的概率就会降为零。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, we've got so many guns in this country that that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我们国家的枪支实在太多了，现实并非如此。

sentences.en: And that's what law enforcement and community folks will say is sometimes they're scared that if you send up somebody, show somebody with a vest and a whistle,
sentences.zh: 这也是执法部门和社区人员会说的话：有时他们会害怕，如果你只派某个人去、只派一个穿着防弹背心、吹着口哨的人去，

sentences.en: that's not going to be enough.
sentences.zh: 那可能根本不够。

sentences.en: So I wish that this were as simple as an ideological slogan.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这能像一条意识形态口号那样简单。

sentences.en: It cannot be.
sentences.zh: 但它不可能那么简单。

sentences.en: But the underlying logic is exactly what you say.
sentences.zh: 不过其背后的逻辑确实如你所说。

sentences.en: If our goal is to keep everybody safe and alive, there are lots of times when a badge and a gun are not the best things to be introducing.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的目标是保证每个人的安全、让人活下来，那么很多时候，警徽和枪并不是最适合带去现场的东西。

sentences.en: You know, I'm reminded of something I read a while ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这让我想起不久前读到的一件事。

sentences.en: After the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国

sentences.en: invasion of Iraq, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 入侵伊拉克之后，美军

sentences.en: military was trying to figure out how troops could be more effective in rebuilding trust with the local community.
sentences.zh: 一直在寻找能让部队更有效地重建与当地社区信任的方法。

sentences.en: And one of the things that General David Petrius eventually concluded was that if you're trying to help people,
sentences.zh: 戴维·彼得雷乌斯将军最终得出的结论之一是，如果你试图去帮助别人，

sentences.en: but you're looking at them through the gun turrets of an armored vehicle,
sentences.zh: 但你却隔着装甲车的枪塔看着他们，

sentences.en: or if you're walking in markets with an M-14 rifle slung from your shoulders, it not only makes it less likely people will trust you,
sentences.zh: 或者你肩膀上斜挎着M-14步枪在集市里巡逻，这不仅让人更难信任你，

sentences.en: it makes it more likely some small incident can end up with a whole lot of people getting shot.
sentences.zh: 还会让一些小摩擦更容易演变成大规模的枪击流血事件。

sentences.en: So it turns out even in military situations, militarized solutions might end up backfiring.
sentences.zh: 所以事实证明，即使在军事行动中，诉诸军事化手段也可能会适得其反。

sentences.en: And of course, if that's true in battle, it has to be triply true when it comes to police working in their communities.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果战场上如此，当警察在自己的社区里执法时，这种道理就更是加倍适用了。

sentences.en: When everyone is tense, everyone is scared, and everyone is armed, even in the absence of malice,
sentences.zh: 当所有人都神经紧绷、心惊肉跳且全副武装时，哪怕主观上完全没有恶意，

sentences.en: the simple laws of probability dictate bad things are going to happen with some regularity.
sentences.zh: 简单的概率规律也注定糟糕的事情会以一定的频率发生。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And the analogy is apt.
sentences.zh: 这个类比非常贴切。

sentences.en: Over the last three decades, we've seen a precipitous decline in violent crime across the United States.
sentences.zh: 在过去的三十家里，我们看到全美范围内的暴力犯罪率急剧下降。

sentences.en: That is the result of a whole bunch of things.
sentences.zh: 这是诸多因素共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: It's community-focused projects.
sentences.zh: 这离不开社区导向的项目。

sentences.en: It is leadership at the local and the state level.
sentences.zh: 离不开地方和州级领导层的努力。

sentences.en: But it's also new techniques in law enforcement of showing up, not arresting the way out of the problem, but showing up to places where violence might happen.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为执法部门采用了新的执勤技术：他们到场时不是靠抓捕来解决问题，而是出现在可能发生暴力事件的地点。

sentences.en: And people tend not to like to do illegal things in the presence of law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 而人们往往不愿意在执法人员面前违法。

sentences.en: Like, that's a portion of it, even though it's definitely not the only, and it may not even be the largest portion of it.
sentences.zh: 这只是其中一部分原因，尽管它绝对不是全部，甚至可能不是最大的一部分。

sentences.en: So if I'm law enforcement and I have worked my behind off to try and reduce the crime level because I thought that was my job,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我是执法人员，我为了降低犯罪率付出了全部心血，因为我认为那是我的职责所在，

sentences.en: and I know that if I'm a chief, I'm definitely getting fired if the crime level goes up, and that's almost the only reason I'm going to get fired.
sentences.zh: 而且我很清楚，如果我是局长，一旦犯罪率上升我肯定会被炒鱿鱼，这几乎是我被炒的唯一原因。

sentences.en: I brought the crime level down.
sentences.zh: 我已经把犯罪率降下来了。

sentences.en: Why don't you love us?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么不爱我们呢？

sentences.en: That's a real thing that law enforcement feels.
sentences.zh: 这是执法人员切实感受到的委屈。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's a response that's untethered to reality.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这种反应是脱离现实的。

sentences.en: It's just untethered to the experiences in black and brown communities where they say,
sentences.zh: 它只是脱离了黑人和棕色人种社区的切身经历，在那些社区里，人们会说：

sentences.en: you have been delivering violence while you've been trying to deliver us from violence.
sentences.zh: 你们在试图拯救我们免受暴力侵害的同时，其实一直在施加暴力。

sentences.en: I find it fascinating that you're effectively addressing problems related to racial disparities in policing without accusing police officers of being bigots.
sentences.zh: 我发现一件很迷人的事，你在没有指责警察是冥顽不灵的偏执狂的情况下，实际上却在解决警务中与种族差异相关的问题。

sentences.en: There's very little finger pointing in your work, right?
sentences.zh: 你的工作很少去指责别人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, so in my day-to-day, when I'm talking with law enforcement, when I'm talking with communities, when I'm talking with my team,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在我的日常工作中，当我与执法部门交流、与社区对话、与我的团队沟通时，

sentences.en: we talk about race and racism a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 我们其实会大量讨论种族和种族主义。

sentences.en: What we don't talk about is whether or not you meant to or are a good person.
sentences.zh: 但我们不讨论的是你到底是不是出于本意、或者你是不是个好人。

sentences.en: We don't talk about character, almost ever.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎从不讨论品格问题。

sentences.en: But everybody who can answer the question, would you like to kill fewer people?
sentences.zh: 但是每个人都能回答这个问题：你愿意少杀几个人吗？

sentences.en: Would you like to be engaged in less racial disparity with the, yes, I would like to do that morally obvious thing?
sentences.zh: 你愿意减少执法过程中的种族差异吗？答案是：是的，我愿意去做这件在道德上显而易见的事。

sentences.en: There are things that can be done, but we don't have to talk about racism the way most people talk about racism.
sentences.zh: 有些事情是可以做的，但我们不需要像大多数人那样去谈论种族主义。

sentences.en: Because the way most people talk about racism is about what kind of person you are.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人谈论种族主义时，讨论的都是你到底是个什么样的人。

sentences.en: And I have found that to be almost entirely irrelevant to making the problem get better.
sentences.zh: 而我发现这对于改善问题几乎毫无用处。

sentences.en: Philip's efforts to reduce racial disparities in policing have been effective.
sentences.zh: 菲利普在减少警务种族差异方面做出的努力卓有成效。

sentences.en: But are they emotionally satisfying?
sentences.zh: 但这些努力在情感上能让人满足吗？

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，我们马上回来。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的脑回路》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的脑回路》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: For years now, working closely with communities and police departments,
sentences.zh: 多年来，耶鲁大学心理学家菲利普·阿蒂巴·高夫一直与社区和警察局紧密合作，

sentences.en: Yale University psychologist Philip Atiba Goff has sought to reduce racial disparities in law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 致力于减少执法过程中的种族差异。

sentences.en: Every time he and his organization, the Center for Policing Equity, go into a community,
sentences.zh: 他和他的机构“警务公平中心”每次进入一个社区时，

sentences.en: they start by looking at the data.
sentences.zh: 都是从查阅数据开始的。

sentences.en: When and where are police using force?
sentences.zh: 警察在什么时候、什么地方使用武力？

sentences.en: What are the specific contexts and situations that make it more likely an officer will reach for a gun?
sentences.zh: 有哪些具体的环境和情况，会让警察更容易把手伸向配枪？

sentences.en: Are there situations that can be safely resolved by someone who doesn't have a badge and a gun?
sentences.zh: 有没有某些情况，其实可以由没有佩戴警徽和枪支的人安全地妥善解决？

sentences.en: Philip, you've worked with the community and the police department in Minneapolis since 2015.
sentences.zh: 菲利普，自2015年以来，你一直与明尼阿波利斯的社区和警察局合作。

sentences.en: You found that in a disproportionate number of situations where police end up using force,
sentences.zh: 你发现，在警察最终动用武力的诸多不成比例的案例中，

sentences.en: there's one particular group of people involved.
sentences.zh: 往往涉及某一个特定的群体。

sentences.en: Who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？

sentences.en: Whenever we're going into a community, the first thing we do is we want to listen to the community.
sentences.zh: 每当我们走进一个社区，我们做的第一件事就是倾听社区的声音。

sentences.en: In Minneapolis, one of the areas that was a concern was homelessness, right?
sentences.zh: 在明尼阿波利斯，人们关心的其中一个领域就是无家可归者问题，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know if you've ever been to Minneapolis, but unless it's June or July, it's cold,
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有去过明尼阿波利斯，但除非是在六月或七月，那里非常冷，

sentences.en: and it sucks to have to be outside and not have a place you can go that's inside.
sentences.zh: 不得不待在室外又没有室内可以去，这种感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: So folks end up in places where they can stay warm.
sentences.zh: 所以人们最后只能去那些能取暖的地方。

sentences.en: But what that also does, it makes people feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 但这样做也会带来一个后果，那就是让人感到不适。

sentences.en: And so they call the police, law enforcement shows up,
sentences.zh: 于是人们报警，执法人员赶到现场，

sentences.en: someone who doesn't have a place to live says,
sentences.zh: 一个没有住所的人会说：

sentences.en: I've not done anything illegal, so they resist law enforcement, and then force ensues.
sentences.zh: 我没做什么违法的的事，于是他们抗拒执法，随后冲突和武力便接踵而至。

sentences.en: You could train law enforcement to recognize that and talk differently about it.
sentences.zh: 你可以训练执法人员去识别这一点，并用不同的方式去沟通。

sentences.en: Or you could give people housing.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以直接给人们提供住房。

sentences.en: This is the thing that is the core of my frustration in doing this work,
sentences.zh: 这正是我从事这项工作时感到核心沮丧所在，

sentences.en: is that oftentimes the only path available to make anything better
sentences.zh: 那就是通常情况下，唯一能够让情况有所改善的途径

sentences.en: is to give something to law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 就是向执法部门让步或提供资源。

sentences.en: But you could just avoid all of this by having a warm place for people to sleep.
sentences.zh: 但你本可以通过为人们提供一个温暖的睡觉地方来避免这一切。

sentences.en: And so when communities, activists within Minneapolis were saying,
sentences.zh: 所以，当明尼阿波利斯的社区和维权人士说：

sentences.en: hey, we need money for this, we provided some data that said,
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们需要这方面的资金，我们便提供了一些数据说：

sentences.en: hey, you should do what the community is asking.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你们应该听从社区的要求。

sentences.en: Take money out of law enforcement, put it into services for unhoused individuals,
sentences.zh: 从执法部门削减资金，将其投入到无家可归者的服务中去，

sentences.en: and you can start to see use of force go down.
sentences.zh: 你就会开始看到武力使用率下降。

sentences.en: So there's something both satisfying and profoundly dissatisfying about your work.
sentences.zh: 所以你的工作既让人感到欣慰，又让人感到深深的挫败感。

sentences.en: It's satisfying because you're making a difference.
sentences.zh: 欣慰是因为你确实带来了改变。

sentences.en: But I think one reason people might feel almost let down by your work
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，人们对你的工作感到有些失望的一个原因，

sentences.en: is it doesn't give us a feeling of moral triumph.
sentences.zh: 在于它并没有给我们带来一种道德胜利的爽感。

sentences.en: By focusing on what's practical,
sentences.zh: 由于专注于务实，

sentences.en: by focusing on areas where police and communities are in consensus,
sentences.zh: 由于专注于警察和社区能够达成共识的领域，

sentences.en: I feel we miss out on the opportunity for moral triumph.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们错失了获得道德胜利的机会。

sentences.en: And that's a feeling we definitely get when we share hot takes on social media.
sentences.zh: 而这种感觉我们在社交媒体上发表激进言论时是绝对能体会到的。

sentences.en: Yes, the work that I do is not designed to satisfy Twitter.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的工作不是为了迎合推特上的情绪而设计的。
